rules.description: Auto-action requires precision >= 0.99. Arithmetic on the scored test set says that is unreachable for threat: 211 positives against 63,767 negatives means a 1% FPR yields ~638 false positives against ~106 true ones. Route to a human instead of relaxing the precision bar.

severe_toxic is an exact subset of toxic in the training labels — no row has severe_toxic=1 with toxic=0. A prediction asserting severe without toxic is logically impossible, so the model is out of distribution and neither head should be trusted. Send it to a human.

The documented failure mode on this corpus is false positives on benign identity mentions. Suppress auto-action in the borderline band so over-enforcement does not concentrate on one group; a human decides.

retired_rules.was: identity_term_present == 1 AND p_max < 0.95 -> human_review, meant to suppress auto-action on borderline identity mentions.
retired_rules.why: Measured on the threshold-selection split (run 20260922T100649877069Z, 31,914 rows): the auto-action thresholds chosen from the 0.99 precision floor are 0.989 (toxic), 0.998 (obscene) and 0.9998 (insult), all above the rule's 0.95 band, so the rule can never intercept an auto-action. Its only effect was to move 1,825 allow-tier comments with an identity term into the human queue, of which 1,683 (92%) had no positive label, cutting queue precision from 0.887 to 0.404. Its premise also did not hold for this model: the false-positive rate among predicted positives was 0.062 with an identity term and 0.065 without (test split: 0.336 vs 0.327). Rules cannot fix a concentration that is not there; a gate can catch one that appears.

auto_action.rationale: auto_action is the only tier that enforces without appeal, and the documented failure mode on this corpus is false positives on benign identity mentions. The 0.99 floor is chosen on the whole selection split and says nothing about this slice: on the selection split of the run named in gates.eval_slice (population tier, auto_action, with an identity term) the slice held 102 of 921 auto-action rows with 2 wrong on the trigger label, a false discovery rate of 0.020 with a 95% interval of 0.005 to 0.069, undetermined against the 0.01 the floor allows. So the slice must clear the floor on its own, at or above the population threshold, before a comment in it is auto-actioned. This replaces rule R103 (see retired_rules): same intent, applied through the threshold machinery instead of a rule.

rules.description: On the scored test set, 211 threat positives against 63,767 negatives would yield about 638 false positives and 106 true positives at an assumed 1% FPR and 50% recall, about 14% precision. This calculation does not rule out 99% precision at a different operating point. As a policy precaution, predictions with p_threat >= 0.30 require a human.

severe_toxic is a subset of toxic in the observed training labels: no row has severe_toxic=1 with toxic=0. Independently fitted heads can violate this relation. Send such predictions to a human for review; the inconsistency alone does not establish distribution shift.

retired_rules.was: identity_term_present == 1 AND p_max < 0.95 -> human_review, meant to suppress auto-action on borderline identity mentions.
retired_rules.why: Measured on the threshold-selection split (31,914 rows). From run 20260922T100649877069Z, made with the rule still active: the auto-action thresholds chosen from the 0.99 floor were 0.989 (toxic), 0.998 (obscene) and 0.9998 (insult), all above the rule's 0.95 band, so the rule could never intercept an auto-action, and because rules override the model tier in both directions its only effect was to move 1,825 allow-tier comments with an identity term into the human queue, of which 1,670 (92%) had no positive label, giving a queue precision of 0.404 and concentrating human scrutiny on the speech it meant to protect. From the run named in gates.eval_slice (same split, same population thresholds, rule removed): the premise check on the population tier (classifier alone, false positive per each tier's own definition), where the false discovery rate among predicted positives was 0.071 with an identity term (15 of 210) and 0.068 without (128 of 1,869), ratio 1.04, 95% interval 0.62 to 1.75: neither confirmed nor excluded for that FDR comparison. It does not establish parity in FPR among truly negative comments. Two replacements were considered. An unconditional cap (identity mentions never auto-actioned) would have turned all 102 identity-term auto-action rows on that split, every one truly positive by some label, into human reviews to prevent about two wrong-trigger enforcements; rejected as a blunt override of the floor-defined tiers. Instead the floor is required on the slice itself (subgroup_thresholds above) and the concentration is measured and gated on every run.

gates.eval_slice: Jigsaw scored test rows (63,978), run 20260922T110655042496Z-baseline, made on the working tree on top of commit e750939f82c7 (manifest git_dirty: true); re-run after committing to refresh.

threshold_selection.definition: identity term = any whole-word match of review_router.signals.IDENTITY_TERMS; predicted positive = routed to auto_action or human_review; false positive = the tier's own definition (triggering label not true for auto_action, no label true for human_review); FDR = false positives / predicted positives; FDR ratio = with-term FDR / without-term FDR with a 95% log-ratio interval. clean_negative_false_positives separately reports FPR = clean comments routed to the tier / all clean comments in that subgroup. allow_false_omission = truly positive allowed comments / all allowed comments.

test.definition: identity term = any whole-word match of review_router.signals.IDENTITY_TERMS; predicted positive = routed to auto_action or human_review; false positive = the tier's own definition (triggering label not true for auto_action, no label true for human_review); FDR = false positives / predicted positives; FDR ratio = with-term FDR / without-term FDR with a 95% log-ratio interval. clean_negative_false_positives separately reports FPR = clean comments routed to the tier / all clean comments in that subgroup. allow_false_omission = truly positive allowed comments / all allowed comments.
